newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks plunge to new 98-mth low at close.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks plunge to new 98-mth low at close.

text.p: Thai stocks fell to new 98-month low on Tuesday after a selloff in bank shares on concerns about the size of their non-performing loans, brokers said.

"Banks led the market losses today on worries about their loan problems. The fall of the SET index below key technical support of 500 points also encouraged other investors to offload shares," said one broker at Ekkapat Finance and Securities.
The SET index ended below the key-500 market, down 13.83 points or 2.70 percent at 497.72 on 3.9 billion baht trade.

Brokers said most banks' and finance companies' non-performing loans which are required to be detailed in their financial statements to the central bank at the end of this quarter were expected to be high due an economic downturn.
"The higher-than-expected non-performing loans will significantly affect banks' and finance companies' earnings," the broker said.
A selloff in banking stocks pulled the sector index down sharply by 5.3 percent. There was some talk that banks were being dumped on the foreign board by some to raise baht funds.
Bangkok Bank fell 10 baht to 122 on the most active trade of 459 million baht.
Thai Farmers Bank slipped six to 83.50 and Krung Thai Bank lost 1.50 to 26.25.
Blue-chip Siam Cement dropped 10 to 420. TelecomAsia eased 1.25 to 25.50.
